title: Reading at Mass
hookLine: proclaiming the word for the people
tomorrow: who said the one who sings prays twice, and did he really say it?

cards: A friend hears you rehearse a speech and says: slow down, nobody can follow. Reading aloud well is harder than it looks. Luke has a scene in a synagogue in Nazareth, Jesus's hometown.

Jesus stands up to read. He's handed the book of the prophet Isaiah, finds the place, and reads. Then he rolls it up, gives it back to the attendant, and sits down, and every eye in the room is on him.
Stand to read, sit to talk. Why the switch?

teach.h: STAND TO READ, SIT TO TEACH.
teach.b: Luke shows the pattern: he stands to read, and he sits to teach. Some readers hear honor in the standing, for words that aren't his own.
Then, seated, his first line is about hearing: "This day is fulfilled this scripture in your ears." In your ears. The scripture happened as it was heard.
That's the job the Church gives the lector, the reader at Mass.

teach.h: GOD SPEAKS WHEN SCRIPTURE IS READ.
teach.b: Its instructions say that when the Scriptures are read in church, God himself speaks to his people. So a lector isn't performing.

A lector lends a voice to words that aren't theirs, standing at the ambo, the place of the word, for people who came to listen. Practical things follow from that. Read it beforehand, out loud, more than once.
Go slower than feels natural, and pause at the end so it can land.
One to tell a friend: when the reading ends, the lector doesn't say the end. The lector says, the word of the Lord, and the people answer, thanks be to God.
And in Luke's scene, Jesus is the reader before he's the preacher.

how: At Mass, lay lectors read the first and second readings from the ambo and end each with 'The word of the Lord'; the people answer 'Thanks be to God.' The Gospel is read by a deacon or priest.

games.q: in the Nazareth synagogue, Jesus has just read from Isaiah. what does Luke say he does next?
o: rolls up the book, sits down, and speaks.
keeps standing and explains each line.
hands the book to Peter to read more.
games.why: he folds the book, gives it back, sits down, and with every eye on him says: this day is fulfilled this scripture in your ears.

practice: Find a short passage, next Sunday's first reading if you can get it, or a psalm, and read it out loud, slowly, as if to a room. Pause at every period. Then read it a second time, slower still, and let one phrase land on you.
If you pray, you can close as a lector does: the word of the Lord.

wordCard.voice: Lector. Latin for reader: the person who proclaims the Scripture readings at Mass, for the people listening. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: a reader. the Church's name for the one who proclaims the readings at Mass.

carryVoice: Your line: lend your voice. The words aren't yours, and that's the honor of it. Off you go.
